content: Bedford Hospital is a District General Hospital located in the town of Bedford, England, and serves the northern and central regions of Bedfordshire. It is managed by the Bedford Hospital NHS Trust. The hospital's primary facilities are situated at the South Wing site. This location includes the Accident and Emergency department, operating theatres, pathology services, inpatient wards, radiology (X-ray) department, oncology services, and outpatient services. Additionally, the South Wing houses BEDOC, which is the Bedford Primary Care Trust's out-of-hours emergency service for general practitioners (GPs). Several significant developments have taken place at the South Wing site in recent years: The Cygnet Wing, opened in 1996, is a dedicated building for paediatric, maternity, and gynaecology services. A new critical care complex was established in 2002. The Macmillan Primrose Centre, an oncology facility funded entirely by charitable donations from the local community, was inaugurated in 2003. Beeden House, which includes a cardiology suite, was opened in 2005. A new pathology building, costing £7 million, was completed in 2005. The South Wing site includes various wards, each serving specific patient needs: Gifford Nash Ward: A medical ward for elderly female patients. John Bunyan Ward: A 16-bed ward for elderly female patients. Meadowbank Ward: A 14-cot Special Care Baby Unit (SCBU) located in the Cygnet Wing. Pilgrim Ward: Specific details not provided in the text. Reginald Hart Ward: A 14-bed ward for female trauma and orthopaedic patients. Richard Wells Ward: A medical ward specializing in respiratory care. Robertson Ward: A 16-bed ward for female patients undergoing major gynaecological or breast surgery. Shand Ward: A 34-bed mixed surgical ward specializing in vascular surgery. Shuttleworth Ward: A 33-bed mixed surgical ward focusing on colorectal and gastrointestinal surgery. Victoria Ward: A 16-bed ward dedicated to stroke patients. Some services are also provided at the North Wing, which is located two miles north of the South Wing. These services include occupational therapy, physiotherapy, rehabilitation facilities, a chest clinic, and a drop-in dental service. Historically, the North Wing housed the hospital's maternity ward, but this was relocated to the South Wing with the opening of the Cygnet Wing in 1996. Psychiatric services are primarily provided at the Weller Wing, which is located on the South Wing site. However, this facility is managed by a separate organization, the Bedfordshire and Luton Mental Health and Social Care Partnership NHS Trust. The psychiatric wards include: Keats Ward: A 24-bed ward for acute adult psychiatry. Brontë Ward: An 18-bed ward for acute adult psychiatry. Chaucer Ward: A 15-bed ward for old-age psychiatry. Milton Ward: A 15-bed ward for old-age psychiatry, focusing on dementia and other organic illnesses. Sheridan Day Hospital: A facility with 15 places per day for patients over the age of 65. In 2001, a scandal emerged regarding the hospital's mortuary. During maintenance work, bodies were stored on the floor of the chapel of rest, leading to public outrage when photographs were published in newspapers and shown on television. An inquiry found the hospital's management at fault, resulting in the resignation of the Chief Executive. For several months, refrigerated trucks were used as temporary mortuaries to prevent further inappropriate storage of deceased bodies. The issue has since been resolved, as the new pathology building now includes a larger mortuary facility.
